description:
MCP server for the AI Patent Search Generator — patent dossiers, prosecution history, Office Action AI analysis, citation/family/CPC lookups, and Google Patents search.

  Works in Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, ChatGPT-with-MCP, and any other MCP-compatible client.

  ## Tools (11)

  - **dossier** — full patent intelligence: bibliographic, claims, citations, family, classifications, examiner stats. 3 credits fresh; free on 24h cache hit.
  - **prosecution** — USPTO file-wrapper documents (Office Actions, responses, amendments). Free.
  - **oa_analyze** — AI analysis of USPTO Office Actions (rejection grounds, cited prior art, suggested response arguments). First 5/application free; 1 credit each thereafter.
  - **search** — multi-strategy patent search against Google Patents (telescoping / onion-ring / faceted). 1 credit.
  - **query** — Boolean query generator (manual paste into Google Patents). 1 credit.
  - **similar** — Google Patents similar-documents ranking. Free.
  - **citations** — backward + forward citation graph, examiner-cited flagged. Free.
  - **family** — patent family (continuations, divisionals, foreign counterparts). Free.
  - **examiner** — name, art unit, allowance rate, average pendency. Free.
  - **cpc** — CPC classification code lookup. Free.
  - **balance** — credit + subscription status. Free.

  Requires an API key minted from the AI Patent Search Generator Chrome extension's Admin tab.

PATENT_SEARCH_API_KEY.title: Patent Search API Key
PATENT_SEARCH_API_KEY.description: API key minted from the AI Patent Search Generator Chrome extension's Admin tab. Format: psg_live_... or psg_test_...

PATENT_SEARCH_API_BASE.title: API Base URL (optional)
PATENT_SEARCH_API_BASE.description: Override the API base URL. Default: https://us-central1-solicitation-matcher-extension.cloudfunctions.net/ai/v1

tool_signatures.name: assignments
tool_signatures.description: Chain of title for a US patent: who owns it now and the recorded assignment history (conveyances, reel/frame, assignor → assignee, dates). Useful for ownership/licensing and M&A due diligence. Free, public-record.

assignments.description: Recorded assignment records (reel/frame, conveyance, dates, assignors, assignees).

tool_signatures.name: attorney
tool_signatures.description: Attorneys/agents of record for a US patent (name + USPTO registration number), plus the docket number and customer number. Useful for competitive intel — who prosecutes for this assignee. Free, public-record.

attorneys.description: Attorneys/agents with name, registration number, and active flag.

customerNumber.description: USPTO customer number associated with the application.

tool_signatures.name: balance
tool_signatures.description: Return the current credit balance and subscription status for the authenticated AI Patent Search Generator account. Use this before calling paid tools (dossier, oa_analyze, query, search) to verify credits are available.

subscription.description: Active subscription plan and status, or null.

subscriptionCredits.description: Credits granted by the active subscription.

tool_signatures.name: challenges
tool_signatures.description: Get the PTAB validity-challenge history for a US patent: who challenged it (petitioner), the patent owner, challenge type (IPR/PGR/CBM), filing/institution dates, and outcome (patent_survived / final_written_decision / terminated). Answers 'was this patent attacked at the PTAB, by whom, and did it survive?'. Free, public-record.

challenges.description: PTAB challenges (trial number, type, petitioner, owner, dates, status, outcome).

tool_signatures.name: citations
tool_signatures.description: Return backward and/or forward citations for a patent. Backward = patents this one cites (its prior art). Forward = patents that cite this one (downstream impact). Each citation includes whether it was examiner-cited (load-bearing on patentability) vs applicant-cited. Free. Lighter payload than `dossier` when you only need citation lists.

direction.description: Which citation set to return. Defaults to 'both'.

cached.description: Whether the result was served from cache.

forward.description: Forward citations with title, assignee, date, and examiner-cited flag.

backward.description: Backward citations with title, assignee, date, and examiner-cited flag.

direction.description: Citation direction returned (backward, forward, or both).

backwardCount.description: Number of backward citations (prior art cited).

parameters.name: direction
parameters.description: Which citation set to return. Defaults to 'both'.

tool_signatures.name: claim_chart
tool_signatures.description: Build a per-claim element chart for a granted US patent. Decomposes each independent claim into discrete elements (preamble, body parts) and maps each element to examiner-cited prior art from cached Office Action analyses. Free when the patent's dossier is already in the 24h cache. Cold dossier fetch costs 3 credits (same as the `dossier` tool). If you also need bibliographic data, citations, or family, prefer `dossier` first — its result is also cached and makes a subsequent `claim_chart` call free. Uses only cached Office Action analyses; to add fresh OA data, call `oa_analyze` first.

patentNumber.description: Publication number in canonical form (e.g. US10867416B2). Loose input like '10,867,416' is normalized.

oaDocumentIds.description: Optional. Restrict the chart to specific Office Action document IDs. If omitted, all cached OAs for this application are used.

cached.description: Whether the result was served from cache (free).

claimCharts.description: Per-claim charts mapping decomposed claim elements to cited prior art.

analyzedOaCount.description: Number of cached Office Actions analyzed for this chart.

parameters.name: oaDocumentIds
parameters.description: Optional. Restrict the chart to specific Office Action document IDs. If omitted, all cached OAs for this application are used.

parameters.name: patentNumber
parameters.description: Publication number in canonical form (e.g. US10867416B2). Loose input like '10,867,416' is normalized.

tool_signatures.name: claims
tool_signatures.description: Fetch just the claims of a patent — the legal scope of the invention, formatted as a numbered list of independent and dependent claims. Much cheaper than `dossier` for LLM token budgets when you only need claim text. Free when the patent's dossier is already in the 24h cache. Cold fetch costs 1 credit (no AI work, just a Google Patents fetch). Prefer this over `dossier` when you don't also need bibliographic data, citations, or family.

patentNumber.description: Publication number in canonical form (e.g. US10867416B2). Loose input like '10,867,416' is normalized.

cached.description: Whether the result was served from cache (free).

claims.description: Claims block: total count, independent claim numbers, and the list of claim items.

parameters.name: patentNumber
parameters.description: Publication number in canonical form (e.g. US10867416B2). Loose input like '10,867,416' is normalized.

tool_signatures.name: company_litigation
tool_signatures.description: Reverse lookup: given a COMPANY name, return all US district-court patent suits it was involved in (as plaintiff or defendant), with the patents, opposing parties, court, and cause. Great for competitive intel / M&A due diligence ('is this company a patent troll or heavily sued?'). If no exact match, returns name suggestions. Coverage 2003-2020.

cases.description: District-court cases with role, court, date, cause, patents, and opposing parties.

caseCount.description: Total number of suits involving the company.

matchedName.description: Canonical name matched in the litigant index.

suggestions.description: Name suggestions when no exact match is found.

displayNames.description: Alternate display names for the matched entity.

asDefendantCount.description: Number of suits where the company was defendant.

asPlaintiffCount.description: Number of suits where the company was plaintiff.

tool_signatures.name: cpc
tool_signatures.description: Look up a Cooperative Patent Classification (CPC) code and return its section, class, subclass, and group context. Accepts any level of code — section letter (e.g. 'H'), class ('H01'), subclass ('H01M'), main group ('H01M10/00'), or subgroup ('H01M10/0525'). Free. v1.0 dataset covers all sections + ~80 common subclasses; subgroup-level descriptions land in v1.1.

code.description: CPC code at any level (section, class, subclass, main group, or subgroup).

section.description: Section-level code and title, or null.

subclass.description: Subclass-level code and title, or null.

mainGroup.description: Main-group-level code and title, or null.

classification.description: Class-level code and title, or null.

uspoBrowserUrl.description: USPTO CPC browser URL for this code.

parameters.name: code
parameters.description: CPC code at any level (section, class, subclass, main group, or subgroup).

tool_signatures.name: cpc_suggest
tool_signatures.description: Suggest CPC (Cooperative Patent Classification) codes from a plain-English description of a technology or invention. Returns 3-5 candidate codes ranked by confidence with reasoning. Use this when you have a product or invention description and want to know which CPC codes to use in patent searches. Costs 1 credit; repeated calls on the same description are cached for 30 days. Coverage note: the curated dataset (~80 common subclasses) covers most software, hardware, and mechanical tech well but may miss niche chemistry/biotech. For looking UP a known code's meaning, use the `cpc` tool instead.

description.description: Plain-English description of the technology or invention. 5-2000 characters. More technical detail yields better suggestions. Examples: 'lithium-ion battery thermal management system', 'machine learning model for fraud detection in payments', 'foldable smartphone hinge mechanism'.

cached.description: Whether the result was served from cache (free).

suggestions.description: Candidate CPC codes with title, confidence, and reasoning.

parameters.name: description
parameters.description: Plain-English description of the technology or invention. 5-2000 characters. More technical detail yields better suggestions. Examples: 'lithium-ion battery thermal management system', 'machine learning model for fraud detection in payments', 'foldable smartphone hinge mechanism'.

tool_signatures.name: dossier
tool_signatures.description: Fetch a comprehensive intelligence dossier for a patent by publication number. Returns bibliographic data (title, assignees, inventors, dates, legal status), independent claims, backward + forward citations, patent family, CPC classifications, examiner info, and similar documents. Costs 3 credits on a fresh fetch; subsequent calls within 24 hours read from cache and are free. The headline tool — most patent-analysis workflows start here.

patentNumber.description: Publication number in canonical form (e.g. US10867416B2, EP3500001B1). Accepts loose input like '10,867,416' or 'us10867416' — the server normalizes.

cached.description: Whether the result was served from the 24h cache (free).

header.description: Bibliographic data: title, assignees, inventors, dates, legal status.

parameters.name: patentNumber
parameters.description: Publication number in canonical form (e.g. US10867416B2, EP3500001B1). Accepts loose input like '10,867,416' or 'us10867416' — the server normalizes.

tool_signatures.name: entity_status
tool_signatures.description: USPTO entity status for a US patent (small / micro / large entity) — a signal of the applicant's size and fee tier. Free, public-record.

smallEntity.description: Whether the applicant claimed small-entity status.

tool_signatures.name: examiner
tool_signatures.description: Get the assigned examiner's name, art unit, total applications handled, allowance rate, and average pendency for a US patent. Free. Useful for prosecution strategy and risk assessment.

totalApplications.description: Total applications handled by the examiner.

tool_signatures.name: family
tool_signatures.description: Return the patent family for a given patent — continuations, divisionals, and national counterparts (foreign equivalents). Useful for confirming worldwide IP coverage and identifying related applications still pending. Free.

cached.description: Whether the result was served from cache.

family.description: Family ID and member list (jurisdiction, publication number, type, status, date).

tool_signatures.name: legal_bundle
tool_signatures.description: Assemble the full legal-intelligence layer for a US patent in one call: PTAB validity challenges, district-court litigation, in-force/maintenance status, chain of title, term/expiration, prosecution timeline, attorneys of record, entity status, and the pre-grant publication. Costs 10 credits on a fresh fetch; subsequent calls within 24 hours read from cache and are free. Prefer this over calling the nine endpoints (challenges, litigation, legal_status, assignments, term, etc.) separately. US patents only.

cached.description: True if served from the 24h cache (free).

tool_signatures.name: legal_status
tool_signatures.description: Is this US patent still in force? Returns in-force vs lapsed/expired, the anticipated 20-year expiration, and the maintenance-fee payment history (derived from USPTO events). Free, public-record.

inForce.description: Whether the patent is in force (true/false/null if unknown).

lapseOrExpirationEvent.description: Lapse/expiration event with date and description, or null.

lastMaintenancePayment.description: Date of the last maintenance-fee payment.

tool_signatures.name: litigation
tool_signatures.description: Get the US district-court infringement litigation history for a patent: who sued whom, in which court, over what (cause of action), with filing dates. Backed by the USPTO Patent Litigation Dataset. Coverage: comprehensive 2003-2016, partial to 2020 (no cases after 2020). Empty result = not litigated on record. Free, public-record.

cases.description: District-court cases (case number, court, date, name, plaintiffs, defendants, cause).

truncated.description: Whether the case list was truncated by the limit.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Max cases to return (default: all stored).

tool_signatures.name: oa_analyze
tool_signatures.description: AI-analyze a USPTO Office Action document to extract rejection grounds (102, 103, 112, etc.), cited prior art, and suggested response arguments. Two invocation forms: (1) pass only `patentNumber` and the server auto-picks the most recent Office Action for the patent; (2) pass both `applicationNumber` and `documentId` (from `prosecution` output) for explicit selection. First 5 analyses per application are free; subsequent analyses cost 1 credit each.

documentId.description: Office Action document ID from prosecution-history output (used with applicationNumber).

patentNumber.description: Patent publication number — auto-picks the most recent OA for this patent.

applicationNumber.description: Application number for explicit selection (used with documentId).

analysis.description: Extracted rejection grounds, cited prior art, and suggested response arguments.

parameters.name: applicationNumber
parameters.description: Application number for explicit selection (used with documentId).

parameters.name: documentId
parameters.description: Office Action document ID from prosecution-history output (used with applicationNumber).

parameters.name: patentNumber
parameters.description: Patent publication number — auto-picks the most recent OA for this patent.

tool_signatures.name: pregrant_pub
tool_signatures.description: The pre-grant publication (as-filed) for a US patent: publication number/date plus the as-filed abstract and claims parsed from the application XML. Useful for comparing as-filed vs as-granted claim scope. Free, public-record.

tool_signatures.name: prosecution
tool_signatures.description: Retrieve the USPTO file-wrapper documents (office actions, responses, amendments, IDS, notices) for a US patent or application. Free. Returns each document's ID, mail date, category, and short description — IDs can be passed to `oa_analyze` for AI analysis.

applicationNumber.description: USPTO application number (e.g. 15912345). One of patentNumber or applicationNumber required.

documents.description: File-wrapper documents (document ID, mail date, category, description).

parameters.name: applicationNumber
parameters.description: USPTO application number (e.g. 15912345). One of patentNumber or applicationNumber required.

parameters.name: patentNumber
parameters.description: Patent publication number (e.g. US10867416B2). One of patentNumber or applicationNumber required.

tool_signatures.name: prosecution_timeline
tool_signatures.description: Full chronological USPTO event log for a US patent's application (filings, office actions, notices, maintenance fees, etc.) — distinct from the 'prosecution' tool which lists file-wrapper documents. Free, public-record.

tool_signatures.name: query
tool_signatures.description: Generate a single optimized Boolean search query for Google Patents from a natural-language description of an invention or technology. Returns one Boolean string only. Use `search` for a multi-strategy set of queries (broad/moderate/narrow) instead. Costs 1 credit.

description.description: Natural-language description of the invention or technology area (e.g. 'foldable smartphone display with ultrasonic fingerprint sensor'). Minimum 10 characters.

optimizedQuery.description: The generated Boolean search query for Google Patents.

parameters.name: description
parameters.description: Natural-language description of the invention or technology area (e.g. 'foldable smartphone display with ultrasonic fingerprint sensor'). Minimum 10 characters.

tool_signatures.name: risk_profile
tool_signatures.description: One-shot patent due-diligence: assemble the legal bundle and return a risk verdict (Low / Moderate / High) with an AI-written rationale — is this US patent in force, battle-tested (survived PTAB), heavily asserted (district-court litigation), and when does it expire? Costs 40 credits on a fresh fetch; 24h cache is free. Risk is framed for a party considering making/selling a product that might read on the patent. Not legal advice.

cached.description: True if served from the 24h cache (free).

verdict.description: riskLabel (Low/Moderate/High), rationale, and the derived signals (inForce, challengeCount, litigationCount, expiration, owner).

tool_signatures.name: search
tool_signatures.description: Generate expert multi-strategy Boolean patent-search queries from a natural-language description. The server (1) extracts technical concepts with synonyms and (2) builds Boolean queries per the chosen strategy, returning them for you to run against your full-text patent engine (e.g. Google Patents). Results are not executed server-side on this API tier (clean USPTO-only surface, no scraping) — run the returned `queries`, or use the `query` tool for a single optimized query. Strategies: 'telescoping' (3 queries: broad/moderate/narrow — recommended default), 'onion-ring' (layered queries adding one concept at a time), 'faceted' (multiple two-concept pair queries). Costs 1 credit.

limit.description: Maximum number of deduplicated hits to return (default 20, max 100).

description.description: Natural-language description of the invention or technology area (minimum 10 characters).

hits.description: Ranked patent hits (only when executed server-side; empty on the client_side API tier).

note.description: Guidance on how to use the returned queries.

queries.description: Boolean queries run with labels and hit counts.

warnings.description: Optional warnings from the search run.

executionMode.description: 'client_side' = run the returned queries yourself (API tier); 'server_side' = hits included.

parameters.name: description
parameters.description: Natural-language description of the invention or technology area (minimum 10 characters).

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of deduplicated hits to return (default 20, max 100).

tool_signatures.name: similar
tool_signatures.description: Return Google Patents' 'similar documents' ranking for a given patent — a list of patents that Google considers technically related based on its own semantic models. Free. Distinct from `search` (which generates new queries from a description); this tool finds patents related to an existing one.

limit.description: Maximum number of similar patents to return (default 20).

cached.description: Whether the result was served from cache.

similar.description: Similar patents with publication number, title, and assignee.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of similar patents to return (default 20).

tool_signatures.name: term
tool_signatures.description: Patent Term Adjustment (PTA) and the resulting adjusted expiration for a US patent: base 20-year expiration, total PTA days, the adjusted expiration, and the A/B/C delay breakdown. Free, public-record.

delayBreakdown.description: A/B/C USPTO delay and applicant delay breakdown.
